-/**
- * `git rev-parse HEAD` resolves in `root` — the one read `verify-cache.ts`'s
- * `treeIdentity` treats as disqualifying. Never throws.
- */
-function headResolves(root: string): boolean {
-  try {
-    return (
-      execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"], {
-        cwd: root,
-        encoding: "utf8",
-        stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"],
-      }).trim() !== ""
-    );
-  } catch {
-    return false;
-  }
-}
-
-/**
- * True when the gate memo (`src/store/verify-cache.ts`) can serve this step, so
- * an unlocked pre-flight makes the in-lock confirm nearly free instead of simply
- * doubling the work.
- *
- * WITHOUT THIS the pre-flight is a pure loss in every mode where the memo cannot
- * answer, and there are two distinct ones:
- *
- *   - `--fresh` and `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` suppress the memo BY DESIGN — they
- *     exist to force a real run. The confirming pass would re-run the suite for
- *     real, inside the lock, for exactly as long as today, with the pre-flight's
- *     own full run added on top.
- *   - A tree git cannot identify suppresses it SILENTLY. `verifyCacheKey`
- *     returns `null` when `git rev-parse HEAD` fails (a repo with no commits, a
- *     directory that is not a repo at all), and `readVerifyPass` /
- *     `writeVerifyPass` then no-op: nothing is recorded, so nothing is reused,
- *     and both passes run the suite for real. Same doubling, reached by a route
- *     that leaves no trace — which is exactly why it has to be checked for here
- *     rather than assumed away.
- *
- * In all of them, keep today's shape: one run, inside the lock.
- *
- * Both tests mirror `verify-cache.ts` (its `disabled()` and the `HEAD` read in
- * its `treeIdentity`); that module owns their meaning and this must not drift
- * from it. Mirrored rather than imported because neither is exported and this
- * fix's frozen boundary does not include widening that module's surface.
- */
-function gateMemoUsable(root: string, opts: AdvanceOptions): boolean {
-  if (opts.fresh === true) return false;
-  const v = process.env["REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE"];
-  if (v !== undefined && v !== "" && v !== "0" && v.toLowerCase() !== "false") return false;
-  return headResolves(root);
-}
-
-/**
- * True when `stage`'s gate is the memoized deterministic gate the pre-flight
- * exists to move out of the lock: redkiln's own `{{redkiln}} verify --grain …`
- * self-invocation (`gates.ts`'s `verifySelfInvocation`, whose shape this
- * mirrors).
- *
- * DELIBERATELY NARROW. A pre-flight runs the gate a second time in the confirming
- * pass, and only this gate has a memo to make that second run free. An arbitrary
- * `run: ./scripts/check.sh` gate has none — pre-flighting it would execute a
- * caller's command twice per advance, which is a side effect no gate author
- * signed up for. Those keep today's behaviour exactly: one run, inside the lock.
- */
-function isMemoizedVerifyGate(stage: Stage): boolean {
-  if (stage.gate?.kind !== "command") return false;
-  const run = stage.gate.run;
-  if (run === undefined) return false;
-  return /\{\{redkiln\}\}\s+verify\b/.test(run) && /--grain\s+(?:story|integration)\b/.test(run);
-}
-
-/**
- * The ONE stage whose gate the unlocked pre-flight may evaluate for this step —
- * or `undefined`, meaning the step keeps today's shape entirely (every gate
- * inside the lock).
- *
- * ONE, not a list, and this is the load-bearing constraint of the whole fix. The
- * pre-flight's only licence is that nothing an observer can see moves: it must
- * refuse with exactly the error the locked pass would have raised, at exactly the
- * point that pass would have raised it, having recorded exactly the telemetry
- * that pass would have recorded. A refusal in the pre-flight means THE LOCKED
- * PASS NEVER RUNS — so anything it would have emitted or committed on the way to
- * that refusal is silently lost. Concretely, the two ways a wider pre-flight
- * breaks that:
- *
- *   - Pre-running two gates. The first passes, the second refuses, and the
- *     first's passing `gate_result` — which the locked pass emits just before it
- *     enters the target stage — is never recorded at all.
- *   - Pre-running a whole `--to` path. A multi-hop walk is INCREMENTAL: cleared
- *     hops are committed, and a later refusal raises `BlockedWalkError`, leaving
- *     the item on the last stage it cleared with its verdict recorded and its
- *     work committed. Refusing up-front collapses that to "nothing happened".

- * the first gate reached:
